weaknesses.critique: The claim is purely about whether total sales and revenues increased year-over-year for Q3 2026, which is directly and unambiguously stated in E2. There is no causal attribution in the claim that needs verification, and the evidence explicitly provides the exact figures ($20.682 billion vs $17.638 billion) and percentage increase (17%). The numeric assertion is straightforward and fully supported.

While the evidence clearly shows an increase in total sales and revenues, I did not examine whether there were any unusual items, one-time events, or accounting changes that might affect the comparability of the periods. However, the claim only asks whether revenues increased, not whether the increase was organic or sustainable, so this does not weaken the verdict of SUPPORTED.

The evidence provided (E2) comes from the same 10-Q filing (accession number 0000018230-26-000057) that covers the period in question, and the figures are presented as part of the consolidated results of operations. There is no indication in any of the evidence passages of restatements or corrections that would call into question the reported figures. The verdict remains appropriately SUPPORTED.
